title: JavaScript Values and First Expressions
summary: Recognize common JavaScript values, observe them in the Console, and evaluate simple expressions that produce new values.

sketchBlocks.title: Text, numbers, and true/false values
Expressions produce new values

quizDraft.title: Spot the boolean
quizDraft.prompt: Which line logs a boolean value?
quizDraft.hint: A boolean is written without quotation marks.

help.hint_1: Strings use quotes; booleans do not.
help.hint_2: Look for the literal value that is exactly `true` or `false`.

quizDraft.title: Find the numeric expressions
quizDraft.prompt: Which expressions produce numbers? Select all that apply.
quizDraft.hint: Choose the expressions JavaScript can evaluate as arithmetic.

help.hint_1: Numbers can participate directly in arithmetic.
help.hint_2: Quoted digits are text, and `false` is a boolean.

quizDraft.title: Read a value type
quizDraft.hint: Compare how JavaScript treats a quoted value with how it treats an unquoted number.

help.concept: using typeof to inspect a value
help.hint_1: The quotation marks are part of the clue; they change how JavaScript interprets the value.
help.hint_2: `typeof` returns a type label, so choose the label that matches quoted text.

quizDraft.title: Follow an expression
quizDraft.prompt: Arrange what happens when JavaScript evaluates `20 + 4` and logs it.
quizDraft.hint: The expression is evaluated before `console.log` displays its result.

help.hint_1: Start with the values and operator.
help.hint_2: The Console can only display the result after JavaScript has produced it.

quizDraft.title: Observe profile values
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: A learner profile can contain different kinds of data, and you need to verify that JavaScript can represent each kind correctly. Task: Use three `console.log` calls to show a favorite color as text, a number of completed lessons, and a boolean that says whether notifications are enabled. Expected result: the Console shows one string, one number, and one boolean value.
quizDraft.hint: Show one text value, one number value, and one boolean value.

help.concept: JavaScript can work with different kinds of values and display them directly in the Console.
help.hint_1: Put the color in quotes, but write the lesson count and boolean without quotes.
help.hint_2: Your three logs should demonstrate text, number, then boolean.

quizDraft.title: Evaluate a score expression
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: A score calculation and a text label can look similar on screen even though JavaScript treats them as different value types. Task: Log the result of `9 + 4`. Then log the type of the number `13` and the type of the text value `"13"`. Expected result: the Console shows `13`, then `number`, then `string`.
quizDraft.hint: Let JavaScript evaluate both the arithmetic expression and each `typeof` operation.

help.concept: Expressions produce values, and `typeof` reports what kind of value JavaScript sees.
help.hint_1: Keep `9 + 4` as an expression instead of replacing it with its result.
help.hint_2: Use `typeof 13` for the number and `typeof "13"` for the quoted text.
